experiment: V-EXP-33 (chart on frame 0, universal daily behaviour) + V-EXP-32 (Kit v2)
hook: Your screen time isn't the real problem. Your pickups are.

frame.want: use the phone less without deleting anything
frame.obstacle: one app opens on autopilot, ~90 pickups a day
frame.cost: 90 pickups x 2 min = 3 hours a day, in pieces

hooks_considered.formula: the check you can do now
hooks_considered.line: Your screen time isn't the real problem. Your pickups are.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y (which app, what to do), muted Y (Screen Time chart, 90 pickups), sendable Y, payoff Y (pause = choice)

hooks_considered.line: Ninety pickups a day. You decided maybe five of them.
hooks_considered.checks: strong but the number reads as a claim about the viewer

hooks_considered.line: Before you delete Instagram, move it. That's the whole fix.
hooks_considered.checks: good, but gives the method away in second 1

beats.hard_truth: Not screen time. Pickups (0.0 s, chart on frame 0)

open_loop.promised: your phone tells you which app pulls you back
open_loop.withheld: what to do with that app (revealed ~30 s)

beats.stakes: 90 pickups a day, 3 hours in pieces
beats.rehook_10: That's ninety times you didn't decide.
beats.interrupt: home-screen icon swiped to the last page
beats.rehook_25: So what do you do with it? (near-silence 1 before)
beats.share_line: Send this to the friend who checks their phone mid-sentence.
beats.follow_reason: Follow for one fix a day. Tonight: the coffee still in you at bedtime (ill-caffeine, 19:30 same day)

note: Screen Time (iOS) really shows Pickups and 'First Used after Pickup'; Android Digital Wellbeing shows unlocks. 90/day and 2 min each are framed as 'say', a worked example, not a statistic. No promise of a specific drop; the claim is a pause where you decide. Different from ill-phone-distance (phone in another room while working).
